newsitem.title: UK: UK roasters still have no plans for price hikes.
newsitem.headline: UK roasters still have no plans for price hikes.

text.p: UK coffee roasters reiterated on Tuesday that they had no plans to raise their retail prices despite increases elsewhere in the European Union.
"We are monitoring the market but we haven't any plans to raise prices," said a spokeswoman for Nestle UK, a unit of Nestle SA.
Whittard of Chelsea, British retailer of gourmet Arabica coffee, also said it wasn't considering a hike.
The renewed strength of the pound sterling against the dollar has cushioned the effect of higher dollar-denominated cost of beans for UK roasters, market analysts said.
But roasters said they were also not entirely convinced if a surge of 40-percent in bean prices since early January could be maintained.
"We are not interested in the short term movements. We are trying to keep retail prices as sustainable as we can to the consumers," said one roaster representative.
"Any price change disrupts consumption and we are trying to avoid that, even if that means taking some pain ourselves," he said.
Earlier on Tuesday, two French roasters took their lead from Germany and Dutch hikes revealing plans to raise their prices.
Industry sources said Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of Philip Morris group, was planning to raise prices of roasted arabica by four francs per kilo from February 25.
Cafes Excella, another French roaster, said it planned a rise of "at least two francs", corresponding to a rise of 23-24 percent current price levels.
"If the rise continues, we are headed for a second round pf retail price hikes in April," said marketing director Jean-Jacques Dothee.
